doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Making a living as a jazz musician then
summary: Times were sometimes hard but players got by and enjoyed playing and sharing ideas.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What was it like to make as living as a jazz musician back at that time? Without getting personal about how much you made and everything, but was it a life that you felt was what you really wanted. Was it easy? Was it hard? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

Both. Times when you’d run out of money it’d be hard. But well the times were different then and it always seemed like you’d get a job someplace, maybe a one-nighter someplace. You’d go out of New York, or you’d get it in New York City, why it seemed like all the guys were getting along real fine. You know, there was no — we’d just play for the enjoyment, too. There was nothing uptight about anything as far as I was concerned. It could be that way nowadays I guess.
Yeah, they say the scene has changed a lot. There’s not as many places to play I guess.
There was a lot of enjoyment then you know.
